terms.comment: The legionary’s shield, of boards covered with leather (Lewis & Short).
The round bronze shield; also neuter, clipeum (Lewis & Short).
Carried by the light infantry and the cavalry; in the poets any shield (Lewis & Short). The diminutive is parmula.

phrases.latin: Gallī occursant in rīpā cum variīs ululātibus cantūque mōris suī, quatientēs scūta super capita
phrases.english: the Gauls came running to meet them on the bank with all kinds of howls and songs in their fashion, shaking their shields above their heads
to have left one’s shield behind is the greatest disgrace
his truth will surround you like a shield

sources: Lewis & Short: scutum · Lewis & Short: clipeus · Lewis & Short: parma
